description: Surfaced by fz-lfp classification. Golden expects {5,80,9,288,...}/368; run+build produce {5,80,14,448,...}/528; interp produces {5,80,10,320,...}/400. Three-path parity violation (run/build vs interp disagree on ALLOCATION COUNTS) plus an upward drift vs the golden (raises need masked-regression scrutiny per convention -- this may be a real allocation regression from the k22.20-23 entry-ownership work, e.g. extra callable-entry thunks). Do NOT rebless upward without root-cause. Repro: fixture_matrix enum_list_allocations.

comments.text: ROOT-CAUSED (2026-07-15, report-only -- correct per no-masked-fix): all drift localized to Enum.reduce (count/member? byte-identical to golden at HEAD). Per-commit attribution: k22.20 regressed single-target dispatch to generic indirect (+20 scalar_box native via unconditional box_scalar_for_any); k22.23 mitigated to +5 but added per-call construction-wrapper structs (+5 native/+1 interp) at a single-member site. Classification: AVOIDABLE WASTE both counters; native is the over-allocating side (per-call re-materialization vs interp amortization). NO point patch -- the fix is the folded-but-never-built k22.24-27 capability, now ticketed as fz-k22.29 (blocks this + fz-5vi). Known-good baseline 6ffdddae7 reproduces golden exactly. Do NOT rebless upward.

RE-SCOPED against HEAD 89db749f6 (2026-08-21). Unblocked -- fz-88t closed, its native objective achieved by the fz-9i4/k22 carrier-authority arc.

The three-way divergence in the title still holds, but the DIRECTIONS FLIPPED and the native side is now the best of the three:

  native (run+build):  {5, 80,  1,  32, 0, 0, 3, 48, 0, 0}  heap 112
  interp:              {5, 80, 10, 320, 0, 0, 3, 48, 0, 0}  heap 400
  golden:              {5, 80,  9, 288, 0, 0, 3, 48, 0, 0}  heap 368

All three lanes print CORRECT values (5 / true / 15). This is purely allocation accounting.

The 2026-07-15 root-cause comment ('run+build produce {5,80,14,448}/528 ... upward drift ... do NOT rebless upward') is SUPERSEDED: native no longer over-allocates at all -- it is EIGHT structs BELOW the golden. The per-iteration {:cont, acc} Deliver envelope is gone from the native path.

REMAINING SCOPE, two parts:
1. INTERP IS THE DEFECT. At 10 structs it is still materializing the envelope on every iteration, where native decomposes into lanes. fz-88t predicted a '+1 by convention' delta for interp; the live delta vs native is +9 -- that is the whole envelope, not a convention. This is the three-path-parity violation this ticket is named for, now isolated to a single path.
2. GOLDEN IS STALE HIGH. 9 -> 1 struct, 288 -> 32 bytes, 368 -> 112 heap. A strict DECREASE, so the rebless is safe by construction (stricter guard) and needs no separate authorization -- but it lands only AFTER interp meets the same floor, so all three paths pin one number.

RISK NOTE: the seven miscompiles that stopped fz-88t (enum_predicate_search wrong values, enum_take_drop_split panic, opaque_fn_value_join/repr_seam raw heap pointers) came from relaxing the NATIVE carrier. That is not what part 1 does -- native is already correct here and must not be touched. The variant-faithfulness hazard still applies to the interp fix: entries dispatching on {:cont, b} vs {:halt, c} need the tag lane plus agreeing lane layouts.

ACCEPTANCE: ela green on run/interp/build against one golden; no other fixture moves (full single-threaded matrix stays at or below 8 red).

IMPLEMENTED -- draft PR 89, commit fb487e423 on fz-66j/interp-tuple-carrier.

ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT WHERE THIS TICKET (or fz-88t) PUT IT. Both pointed at the delivered-value binding path. Instrumenting make_tuple_on_proc with a backtrace settled it empirically: all 18 DeliveredResume layouts in enum_list_allocations already carry carrier: Absent, so bind_delivered_value/project_backend_value_for_contract were already taking the decomposed lane path. Aggregating 542 traced tuple allocations by caller frame: 541 from make_tuple (i.e. ProgramStep::Tuple) and 1 from materialize_transport_value. The envelopes were built one step EARLIER than either ticket assumed, at tuple construction.

THE FIX: ProgramStep::Tuple materialized unconditionally; native's BackendStep::Tuple (jobs/native.rs:1019) has always consulted the value layout first and binds Transport{shape, lanes} when the carrier is not ValueRef. New helper tuple_step_value reads the same layout. No new fact, no new concept -- one more reader of the carrier authority instead of a second opinion. make_tuple lost its last caller and was deleted.

TDD: compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_reduce_envelope_materialization (drive_test.rs) -- JIT 1 vs interp 8 at HEAD, equal after.

RESULT: matrix 8 red -> 4. ela green on all three paths at {5,80,1,32,0,0,3,48,0,0}/112. tree green on all three -- fz-bt1 CLOSED, same root cause. Survivors (fz-qe0, fz-f98.14 x2, fz-km1) all pre-existing and untouched.

REBLESSED DOWNWARD, each a strict decrease with byte-identical output, each moving interp ONTO native's existing number: ela struct 9->1 (368->112); enum_sort::interp 10->0 (1808->1488); quicksort::interp 11->0 (1264->912); enum_reduce_suspend::interp 2->1 (80->48). quicksort's README has pinned struct_allocs = 0 as the native target all along and interp now hits it.

SIDE EFFECTS RECORDED ON THEIR OWN TICKETS, not fixed here: fz-9lj (enum_reduce_suspend identity #fn<3/0> -> #fn<2/0>, allocation-order schema id, arity unaffected) and fz-1yo (enum_sort.expected.diagnostics gutter shift from a README edit).

GATES: lib 1440/0; matrix 406/4 single-threaded; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets 0 warnings; fmt clean.

title: enum_list_allocations: THREE-WAY allocation divergence -- run/build vs interp vs golden all disagree
